transcript.text: We just got an incredibly rare video out of Alaska, and trust me, policing out there is a whole different ballgame. The Fairbanks area-wide narcotics team, Alaska Criminal Suppression Unit, state troopers and other authorities tracked a suspected drug trafficker for over a week. A search warrant approved the day before allowed detail electronic surveillance for weapons, narcotics, documents, and currency. 45-year-old Michael Glymes and 42-year-old Melody Perry were convicted felons, believed to be armed and dangerous. When a tracker showed the suspect vehicle leaving Anchorage for Fairbanks to allegedly trafficked drugs, Agency stays 250 miles away past a remote stretch of parks highway and set up stopsticks in anticipation of a pursuit. After 40 miles of undercover tailing, Mark Cruises emerged from a church parking lot to conduct a felony stop. I see brake lights there shopping. Go, go, go, go. To the post-incident report, the stopsticks deflated both front tires, but officers were unaware at first due to the suspect's continued high speeds. This chase, officers are using the police helicopter Helo 2 to track the suspect. and airlift anyone needing emergency medical care. This shotgun wad appears to fly out the windshield before losing velocity to boomerang back into the cruiser at the officer. The suspect fires his gun again, causing officers to fire back. I see moving on passenger, hey, passenger! No south of them? Yep. The guns. They'll cut them up. We got him out. He's still bleeding, he's still breathing, he's still breathing. For all medic. Make sure there's no other guns. guns, I'm going off record. Now, the female's in here. I didn't take any shots. Okay, that's what matters. We'll have somebody talk to the second, did I get some water or anything like that? Okay. I want to make sure that you're not injured. Are you injured at all? Okay. Unintrusive as I possibly can, but there are times where people are injured and they don't know about it. So I'm going to unbuckle this. I'm just going to check your back here. Good there. It's going to be just a little while. That's a bad question to ask. Are you okay right now? physically or your opinion you i won't fall right to be part of that i'm going to put you in a helicopter and the helicopter's going to take you up to fairbanks so you can talk to the investigators there or whatever but i do think you can talk to you talk to you yes i don't mind you know report state michael had two handgun magazines and a baton on him with bullet wounds to his right shoulder blade and the top left of his head melody perry was flown back to fair for questioning aboard Hilo 2, which landed on the highway for the nearly 40-minute transport to Fairbanks. Michael had a lengthy criminal history, including multiple sexual assault charges and a violent assault conviction for pouring acid on his wife's face. When officers contacted his wife over 2,500 miles away in Texas, she said they hadn't spoken in about six months. According to the police report, she had previously changed her name to Michael Grimes, matching her now deceased husband's name, but was in the process of changing it back. changing it back. Reports state suspects Michael and Melody were in an intimate relationship. She told officers he ordered her to get on the floor of the vehicle just before he initially fired. In the days that followed, a search of the vehicle found multiple guns, 2.678 kilos or 5.9 pounds of methamphetamines, 257.5 grams or 9 ounces of fentanyl powder, 111 grams, or 3.92 ounces, in about 1,000 blue fentanyl pills, drug paraphernalia indicating distribution, hundreds of rounds of mixed caliber ammunition and over $6,300 in cash. The truck's damage showed bullet fragments on the tailgate, with shots traveling from the back window to the windshield and fragments in the driver's side headrest. Four officers fired their weapons during the incident, prompting a deadly force investigation. No officers were harmed in this video, despite multiple cruisers taking gunfire. Though officers and news sources initially reported Michael was shot and killed by police, his autopsy confirmed he died from his own handgun. Forensic bullet trajectory matched his hat. the truck's roof. According to the police report, Melody claimed his final words were to tell police whatever they wanted to know. Police notified Michael's daughter as next of kin. The report notes a text she sent to officers. I feel really bad for the troopers. I don't want them to lose sleep at night. Our family speculated for quite some time that when his actions caught up to him, that death by cop would be a very possible course of action. Breaks my heart that he was too cowardly to face the consequences of his actions and chose to put that burden on law enforcement. I want them to know this was a choice he made, and we are thinking of them and their families during this time. He was on borrowed time, and it was inevitable. In this case, Melody was charged with one count of felon in possession of a weapon. Beyond her actions in the video, officers also obtained footage of her and Michael openly carrying and buying firearm accessories at Alaska Ammo, footage that contributed to the approved search warrant and felony stop. Investigators found the weapons they were armed with were bought by a third party at Sportsman's Warehouse, by an acquaintance who illegally purchased them under their own name. A search of Michael's home uncovered the receipt with a handwritten note reading, Happy Anniversary Mike and Mel, and, hers purple, his white, matching the description of the handguns found on scene. Surveillance also showed the purchase with the third party, presumably using a card in their own name. The purchaser was indicted on one count of making a false statement during a firearm purchase. The report also suggests others may have bought weapons for the pair, though this remains unconfirmed. According to the Alaska Department of Corrections, Melody was sentenced for one count of felon in possession of a weapon and was incarcerated. Her release is scheduled to coincide with the publishing of this video.
